text: check_censoring_dgm() compares three censoring summaries DGM reference data (dgm$df_super) simulated dataset: overall censoring rate, censoring-time quantiles among censored subjects, KM-based median censoring time (estimated reversing event indicator censored observations become “event” interest). Reading output. Flags warn absolute censoring-rate discrepancy exceeds rate_tol (default 10 percentage points) KM median censoring times differ median_tol (default 25%). Common causes: Time-scale mismatch — check exp(dgm$model_params$mu) analysis_time. Short analysis_time — administrative censoring dominates censoring process, inflating censoring rate compressing censoring times. Large cens_adjust — log-scale shift moved DGM censoring distribution far original data.

text: calibrate_cens_adjust() uses uniroot find value cens_adjust — log-scale shift applied DGM censoring model — equates chosen summary statistic reference simulated data. Two targets available: "rate" (overall censoring rate) "km_median" (KM-based median censoring time). objective function works. candidate cens_adjust: simulate_from_dgm() generates n_eval synthetic subjects. check_censoring_dgm() extracts target metric. objective returns sim_metric - ref_metric. uniroot finds zero crossing. fixed seed inside objective ensures candidate always evaluated identically, preventing root-finder chasing Monte Carlo noise. Monotonicity note. objective monotone cens_adjust targets: larger values increase censoring times (lower rate, higher KM median), smaller values opposite. uniroot fails, target lies outside interval; widen retry.

text: null DGM built, diagnosed, calibrated, simulated trial single call simulate_from_dgm(). function samples super population replacement, assigns treatment, generates latent survival times AFT model, applies calibrated censoring model, truncates analysis_time. single-trial example illustrates output structure. null DGM every patient true HR 0.70, flag_harm always 0 — embedded subgroup. 149 replications drive extreme-subgroup analysis Part IV follow pattern, looping subgroups inside replicate.
code:
sim_data <- simulate_from_dgm(   dgm           = dgm,   n             = 600,   rand_ratio    = 1,   analysis_time = 84,   max_entry     = 24,   cens_adjust   = cal$cens_adjust,   seed          = 100 )  cat("Simulated trial:  N =", nrow(sim_data), "
") ## Simulated trial:  N = 600 cat("Treatment allocation:",     table(sim_data$treat_sim)[["0"]], "control /",     table(sim_data$treat_sim)[["1"]], "experimental
") ## Treatment allocation: 300 control / 300 experimental cat("Overall event rate :", round(mean(sim_data$event_sim), 3), "
") ## Overall event rate : 0.412 cat("Event rate (harm subgroup):",     round(mean(sim_data$event_sim[sim_data$flag_harm == 1]), 3), "
") ## Event rate (harm subgroup): 0.57 cat("Event rate (no-harm)      :",     round(mean(sim_data$event_sim[sim_data$flag_harm == 0]), 3), "
") ## Event rate (no-harm)      : 0.374 library(survival)  # KM for overall, harm subgroup, and complementary subgroup km_all  <- survfit(Surv(y_sim, event_sim) ~ treat_sim,                    data = sim_data) km_harm <- survfit(Surv(y_sim, event_sim) ~ treat_sim,                    data = subset(sim_data, flag_harm == 1)) km_noharm <- survfit(Surv(y_sim, event_sim) ~ treat_sim,                      data = subset(sim_data, flag_harm == 0))  # Quick summary of true vs observed HRs cox_all   <- coxph(Surv(y_sim, event_sim) ~ treat_sim, data = sim_data) cox_harm  <- coxph(Surv(y_sim, event_sim) ~ treat_sim,                    data = subset(sim_data, flag_harm == 1)) cox_noharm <- coxph(Surv(y_sim, event_sim) ~ treat_sim,                     data = subset(sim_data, flag_harm == 0))  results_df <- data.frame(   Subgroup   = c("ITT", "Harm (true)", "No-harm (true)"),   N          = c(nrow(sim_data),                  sum(sim_data$flag_harm == 1),                  sum(sim_data$flag_harm == 0)),   True_HR    = round(c(dgm$hazard_ratios$overall,                        dgm$hazard_ratios$harm_subgroup,                        dgm$hazard_ratios$no_harm_subgroup), 3),   Observed_HR = round(exp(c(coef(cox_all),                              coef(cox_harm),                              coef(cox_noharm))), 3) ) print(results_df) ##         Subgroup   N True_HR Observed_HR ## 1            ITT 600   0.781       0.984 ## 2    Harm (true) 114   1.206       2.232 ## 3 No-harm (true) 486   0.729       0.782

Fit stratified Cox, return c(HR point estimate, upper 95% CI bound) cox_sR <- function(data) {   fit <- tryCatch(     coxph(Surv(y_sim, event_sim) ~ treat_sim + strata(grade), data = data),     error = function(e) NULL   )   if (is.null(fit) || nrow(summary(fit)$conf.int) == 0)     return(c(NA_real_, NA_real_))   ci <- summary(fit)$conf.int[1, ]   c(ci["exp(coef)"], ci["upper .95"]) }  # Storage: HR point estimates and upper 95% confidence bounds sim_hrs <- matrix(NA_real_, n_sims_null, n_sg, dimnames = list(NULL, sg_names)) sim_ubs <- matrix(NA_real_, n_sims_null, n_sg, dimnames = list(NULL, sg_names)) sim_ns  <- matrix(NA_real_, n_sims_null, n_sg, dimnames = list(NULL, sg_names))  for (ss in seq_len(n_sims_null)) {    df_s <- simulate_from_dgm(     dgm           = dgm_null,     n             = nrow(gbsg),     analysis_time = 84,     max_entry     = 24,     cens_adjust   = cal_null$cens_adjust,     seed          = ss   )   df_s$flag_itt <- 1L    # Make quantile cut-points available as scalar variables in the eval   # environment so expressions like "size <= size_med" resolve correctly.   # Expose scalar cut-points as columns so subset expressions resolve.   df_s$age_med  <- age_med   df_s$size_med <- size_med   df_s$nodes_q3 <- nodes_q3   df_s$pgr_med  <- pgr_med   df_s$er_cut   <- er_cut    # Regenerate random benchmark subgroups for this simulated trial.   # Random subgroups are re-sampled each iteration: their purpose is to   # benchmark the variability of a subgroup of a given size with no true   # treatment effect heterogeneity — exactly what each simulated trial provides.   set.seed(ss + 1e6L)   n_s   <- nrow(df_s)   r_idx <- sample.int(n_s, min(60L, n_s), replace = FALSE)   df_s$random60 <- as.integer(seq_len(n_s) %in% r_idx)   df_s$random40 <- as.integer(seq_len(n_s) %in% r_idx[seq_len(min(40L, length(r_idx)))])   df_s$random20 <- as.integer(seq_len(n_s) %in% r_idx[seq_len(min(20L, length(r_idx)))])   df_s$random15 <- as.integer(seq_len(n_s) %in% r_idx[seq_len(min(15L, length(r_idx)))])    for (gg in seq_len(n_sg)) {     df_sg <- tryCatch(       subset(df_s, eval(parse(text = sg_ids[[gg]]))),       error = function(e) NULL     )     if (is.null(df_sg) || nrow(df_sg) < 5) next     sim_ns[ss, gg] <- nrow(df_sg)     r <- cox_sR(df_sg)     sim_hrs[ss, gg] <- r[1]     sim_ubs[ss, gg] <- r[2]   } }  cat("Simulations completed:", n_sims_null, "\n") ## Simulations completed: 149

ForestSearch results: Q̂\widehat{Q} = Preanti ≤\le 744.5 Age >> 34 (consistency 92.8%) θ̂*(Q̂)=0.59\hat{\theta}^*(\widehat{Q}) = 0.59 (0.37, 0.94) — 382 subjects (35%) θ̂*(Q̂c)=0.95\hat{\theta}^*(\widehat{Q}^c) = 0.95 (0.65, 1.41) — 701 subjects (65%) bias-corrected estimate suggests relatively strong benefit (0.59 vs 0.84 ITT) statistically significant. Cross-validation: N-fold CV reproduced full analysis subgroup definition 7 1,083 training sets. N-fold predicted Cox estimate 0.59 (0.37, 0.94), identical bootstrap bias-corrected estimate. Across 200 random 10-fold analyses, median 9/10 folds identified subgroup sensCV(Q̂)≈69%\text{sensCV}(\widehat{Q}) \approx 69\%. Biological plausibility: finding aligns HIV Trialists’ Collaborative Group meta-analysis reporting greater treatment effects among participants previous antiretroviral therapy higher baseline CD4 counts. what: Step 1: Create a Data Generating Mechanism (DGM)
title: Simulation Studies for Evaluating ForestSearch Performance
text: DGM defines ground truth simulation. Building GBSG breast cancer dataset covariate template, setup_gbsg_dgm() fits Accelerated Failure Time (AFT) model Weibull baseline hazard generates super-population potential outcomes. Key decisions stage: Hypothesis: model = "alt" introduces treatment effect heterogeneity (harm subgroup H vs. benefit complement Hc); model = "null" imposes uniform treatment effect true subgroup exists (type-error evaluation). Effect size: k_inter parameter scales treatment--covariate interaction. Rather setting manually, use calibrate_k_inter() find value achieves target HR harm subgroup, calibrated either Cox HR (use_ahr = FALSE) average hazard ratio (use_ahr = TRUE). Subgroup definition: default, H = {low estrogen receptor premenopausal} (z1 = 1 & z3 = 1), covering roughly 13% super-population. Censoring: Weibull uniform censoring, optionally adjusted via cens_adjust control overall event rate. resulting DGM object stores super-population, true hazard ratios (Cox-based AHR), individual-level potential outcomes (loghr_po), model parameters needed downstream simulation.

Carries forward true subgroup indicator flag_harm individual loghr_po evaluation. ForestSearch uses random-split consistency evaluation, simulated trial independent replicate full analysis pipeline.

title: Simulation Studies for Evaluating ForestSearch Performance
text: generate_aft_dgm_flex() general DGM builder. requires analyst supply dataset make every modelling choice explicitly. GBSG DGM setup_gbsg_dgm() equivalent following call — simply automates preparation: setup_gbsg_dgm() preferred GBSG simulation setting guarantees exact replication León et al. (2024) covariate construction subgroup definition without requiring analyst reproduce preparation steps hand.
code: library(forestsearch) library(survival)   # for survival::gbsg  # ── Step 1: Prepare the GBSG dataset ──────────────────────────────────────  dfa <- survival::gbsg  # Convert time to months (matching León et al.) dfa$y     <- dfa$rfstime / 30.4375 dfa$treat <- dfa$hormon  # Subgroup-defining binary variables # H = {ER ≤ 25th percentile} ∩ {premenopausal} er_cut <- quantile(dfa$er, probs = 0.25) dfa$z1 <- as.factor(ifelse(dfa$er  <= er_cut, 1L, 0L))  # ER low dfa$z2 <- as.factor(ifelse(dfa$age <= median(dfa$age), 1L, 0L)) dfa$z3 <- as.factor(ifelse(dfa$meno == 0, 1L, 0L))       # premenopausal dfa$z4 <- as.factor(ifelse(dfa$pgr  <= median(dfa$pgr), 1L, 0L)) dfa$z5 <- as.factor(ifelse(dfa$nodes <= median(dfa$nodes), 1L, 0L)) dfa$v6 <- as.factor(ifelse(dfa$size  <= median(dfa$size), 1L, 0L)) dfa$v7 <- as.factor(ifelse(dfa$grade == 3, 1L, 0L))  # ── Step 2: Call generate_aft_dgm_flex() ──────────────────────────────────  dgm_flex <- generate_aft_dgm_flex(   data            = dfa,   outcome_var     = "y",   event_var       = "status",   treatment_var   = "treat",   # Analyst-visible covariates (what FS will search over)   continuous_vars = character(0),    # all pre-discretised   factor_vars     = c("z1", "z2", "z3", "z4", "z5", "v6", "v7"),   # Subgroup definition: H = {z1 = 1} ∩ {z3 = 1}   subgroup_vars   = c("z1", "z3"),   subgroup_cuts   = list(z1 = 1, z3 = 1),   # both must equal 1   # Treatment effect structure   model   = "alt",   k_inter = 2.5,   k_treat = 1.0,   n_super = 5000,   seed    = 8316951 )

code: t0 <- proc.time()[3]  # Create DGM with heterogeneous treatment effect # HR in harm subgroup (H) will be > 1 (treatment harmful) # HR in complement (H^c) will be < 1 (treatment beneficial)  dgm_alt <- setup_gbsg_dgm(   model = "alt",   k_treat = 1.0,   k_inter = 2.0,      # Interaction effect multiplier   k_z3 = 1.0,   z1_quantile = 0.25, # ER threshold at 25th percentile   n_super = 5000,   cens_type = "weibull",   seed = 8316951,   verbose = TRUE )  # Enrich DGM with CDE values (computed from super-population theta_0/theta_1) dgm_alt <- compute_dgm_cde(dgm_alt)  # Examine the DGM (print method now shows both HR and AHR metrics) print(dgm_alt) ## GBSG-Based AFT Data Generating Mechanism (Aligned) ## =================================================== ##  ## Model type: alt  ## Super-population size: 5000  ##  ## Effect Modifiers: ##   k_treat: 1  ##   k_inter: 2  ##   k_z3: 1  ##  ## Hazard Ratios (Cox-based, stacked PO): ##   Overall (causal): 0.7331  ##   Harm subgroup (H): 2.9651  ##   Complement (Hc): 0.6612  ##   Ratio HR(H)/HR(Hc): 4.4846  ##  ## Average Hazard Ratios (from loghr_po): ##   AHR (overall): 0.7431  ##   AHR_harm (H): 3.8687  ##   AHR_no_harm (Hc): 0.5848  ##   Ratio AHR(H)/AHR(Hc): 6.6157  ##  ## Subgroup definition: z1 == 1 & z3 == 1 (low ER & premenopausal)  ## ER threshold: 8 (quantile = 0.25) ## Subgroup size: 634 (12.7%) ## Analysis variables: v1, v2, v3, v4, v5, v6, v7 timings$dgm_creation <- proc.time()[3] - t0

text: core computation handled make_est_row() helper: Key formulas — Relative Bias: b† column always appears; measures percentage bias versus DGM’s marginal/causal HR (θ†). CDE values available, second column b‡ prepended, measuring bias versus controlled direct effect (θ‡). dual-column layout matches Bias_dagger / Bias_ddagger columns Table 5 Leon et al. (2024). Positive values indicate upward bias (common naive Cox HR data-driven subgroups due selection bias).
code: make_est_row <- function(estimates, true_val, label, cde_val = NA_real_) {   est <- estimates[!is.na(estimates)]   # drop any NA estimates   if (length(est) == 0) return(NULL)    avg_est  <- mean(est)   sd_est   <- sd(est)   min_est  <- min(est)   max_est  <- max(est)    # b-dagger: bias relative to marginal (causal) truth   b_dagger <- 100 * (avg_est - true_val) / true_val    row <- data.frame(     Estimator    = label,     Avg          = round(avg_est, digits),     SD           = round(sd_est, digits),     Min          = round(min_est, digits),     Max          = round(max_est, digits)   )    if (has_cde && !is.na(cde_val)) {     # b-ddagger: bias relative to CDE truth     b_ddagger <- 100 * (avg_est - cde_val) / cde_val     row[["b-ddagger (%)"]] <- round(b_ddagger, digits)     row[["b-dagger (%)"]]  <- round(b_dagger, digits)   } else {     row[["b-dagger (%)"]]  <- round(b_dagger, digits)   }   row } b† (%)  = 100 * (mean(theta-hat) - theta†) / theta†     [marginal truth] b‡ (%)  = 100 * (mean(theta-hat) - theta‡) / theta‡     [CDE truth]

what: Comparing Vignette Results with Published Benchmarks
title: Simulation Studies for Evaluating ForestSearch Performance
text: running full 20,000-simulation study, can place vignette’s build_classification_table() output alongside reference tables assess reproducibility. Key comparisons: Type error control: (H) row null scenarios close reference values (e.g., FSl: 0.02, FSlg: 0.03 M1). Power: (H) row alternative scenarios (e.g., FSlg: 0.86 M1 Alt) serves detection benchmark. Classification accuracy: sens(H) ppv(H) values indicate well method recovers true subgroup boundary. Estimation bias (b†): bias-corrected estimator theta-hat*(H-hat) reduce upward bias seen plugin theta-hat(H-hat) relative marginal truth θ†. CDE bias (b‡): CDE values populated DGM, b‡ column provides complementary view bias relative controlled direct effect θ‡. θ‡ θ† generally differ (Jensen’s inequality), two bias columns offer different perspectives estimator accuracy. reference Table B2, note b‡ can negative b† positive estimator, reflecting gap two truth targets. Note exact replication requires DGM calibration, censoring rate, random seeds. vignette’s reduced simulation count (n_sims = 1000) show higher Monte Carlo variability published 20,000-simulation results.

code: library(forestsearch)  # --- Step 1: Run ForestSearch --- fs <- forestsearch(   df.analysis     = trial_data,   outcome.name    = "tte",   event.name      = "event",   treat.name      = "treat",   confounders.name = c("age", "biomarker", "stage", "region"),   sg_focus        = "maxSG",   hr.threshold    = 1.25,   hr.consistency  = 1.0,   pconsistency.threshold = 0.90,   fs.splits       = 400,   use_lasso       = TRUE,   use_grf         = TRUE,   parallel_args   = list(plan = "multisession", workers = 4) )  print(fs) summary(fs)  # --- Step 2: Bootstrap Bias Correction --- fs_bc <- forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture(   fs.est    = fs,   nb_boots  = 2000,   parallel_args = list(plan = "multisession", workers = 6) )  # Publication-ready tables summaries <- summarize_bootstrap_results(fs_bc) summaries$main_table_gt  # --- Step 3: Cross-Validation --- # K-fold CV (repeated 10-fold) fs_cv <- forestsearch_tenfold(   fs.est  = fs,   sims    = 200,   Kfolds  = 10,   parallel_args = list(plan = "multisession", workers = 6) )  cv_metrics_tables(fs_cv)  # N-fold (leave-one-out) CV fs_oob <- forestsearch_Kfold(   fs.est  = fs,   Kfolds  = nrow(trial_data),   parallel_args = list(plan = "multisession", workers = 6) )  # --- Step 4: Visualization --- # Forest plot with bias-corrected estimates and CV metrics plot_subgroup_results_forestplot(   fs_results  = list(fs.est = fs, fs_bc = fs_bc, fs_kfold = fs_cv),   df_analysis = trial_data,   outcome.name = "tte",   event.name   = "event",   treat.name   = "treat" )  # Weighted Kaplan-Meier curves by subgroup plot_sg_weighted_km(fs, fs_bc = fs_bc)

title: Bootstrap Results for ForestSearch with Bias Correction — bootstrap_results
text: Two bias correction approaches implemented: Method 1 (Simple Optimism): $$H_{adj1} = H_{obs} - (H^*_{*} - H^*_{obs})$$ \(H^*_{*}\) new subgroup HR bootstrap data \(H^*_{obs}\) new subgroup HR original data. Method 2 (Double Bootstrap): $$H_{adj2} = 2 \times H_{obs} - (H_{*} + H^*_{*} - H^*_{obs})$$ \(H_{*}\) original subgroup HR bootstrap data. : H_obs: Original subgroup HR original data H_star: Original subgroup HR bootstrap data Hstar_obs: New subgroup (found bootstrap) HR original data Hstar_star: New subgroup (found bootstrap) HR bootstrap data

title: Calibrate Censoring Adjustment to Match DGM Reference Distribution — calibrate_cens_adjust
text: Two calibration targets supported: "rate" Overall censoring rate (proportion censored). Finds cens_adjust mean(event_sim == 0) simulated data equals mean(event == 0) dgm$df_super. "km_median" KM-based median censoring time, estimated reversing event indicator censored observations become "event" interest. Finds cens_adjust simulated KM median matches reference KM median.

title: Calibrate Censoring Adjustment to Match DGM Reference Distribution — calibrate_cens_adjust
text: candidate cens_adjust value, objective function: Calls simulate_from_dgm() n = n_eval candidate cens_adjust. Calls check_censoring_dgm() verbose = FALSE extract target metric. Returns sim_metric - ref_metric. uniroot finds zero crossing, .e. cens_adjust simulated reference metrics equal.

title: Calibrate Censoring Adjustment to Match DGM Reference Distribution — calibrate_cens_adjust
text: objective monotone cens_adjust targets: Larger cens_adjust → longer censoring times → lower censoring rate higher KM median. Smaller cens_adjust → shorter censoring times → higher censoring rate lower KM median. uniroot fails (target lies outside search interval), boundary values printed wider interval tried.

title: Calibrate Censoring Adjustment to Match DGM Reference Distribution — calibrate_cens_adjust
text: objective function involves simulation, Monte Carlo noise. Setting fixed seed sufficiently large n_eval (>= 2000) reduces noise enough reliable root-finding. tol argument controls root-finding tolerance cens_adjust scale (metric scale).

title: Diagnose Censoring Consistency Between DGM Source Data and Simulated Data — check_censoring_dgm
text: reference censoring distribution derived dgm$df_super, sampled replacement data passed generate_aft_dgm_flex(). Columns y (observed time) event (event indicator) df_super reflect original observed censoring process DGM time scale. KM median censoring time estimated reversing event indicator (1 - event), treating events censored censored observations event interest. gives non-parametric estimate censoring time distribution unconfounded event occurrence. Common causes discrepancy: (1) time-scale mismatch (DGM built days, analysis_time months); check exp(dgm$model_params$mu) analysis_time. (2) Large cens_adjust shifting censoring substantially fitted model. (3) Short analysis_time time_eos making administrative censoring dominate censoring process.

title: Create GBSG-Based AFT Data Generating Mechanism — create_gbsg_dgm
text: model Character. Either "alt" alternative hypothesis heterogeneous treatment effects, "null" uniform treatment effect. Default: "alt" k_treat Numeric. Treatment effect multiplier applied treatment coefficient fitted AFT model. Values > 1 strengthen treatment effect. Default: 1 k_inter Numeric. Interaction effect multiplier treatment-subgroup interaction (z1 * z3). used model = "alt". Higher values create heterogeneity HR(H) HR(Hc). Default: 1 k_z3 Numeric. Effect multiplier z3 (menopausal status) coefficient. Default: 1 z1_quantile Numeric. Quantile threshold z1 (estrogen receptor). Observations ER <= quantile coded z1 = 1. Default: 0.25 n_super Integer. Size super-population empirical HR estimation. Default: 5000 cens_type Character. Censoring distribution type: "weibull" "uniform". Default: "weibull" use_rand_params Logical. TRUE, modifies confounder coefficients using estimates randomized subset (meno == 0). Default: FALSE seed Integer. Random seed super-population generation. Default: 8316951 verbose Logical. Print diagnostic information. Default: FALSE

title: Create GBSG-Based AFT Data Generating Mechanism — create_gbsg_dgm
text: AFT model uses covariates: treat, z1, z2, z3, z4, z5, ("alt") interaction zh = treat * z1 * z3.

title: Create GBSG-Based AFT Data Generating Mechanism — create_gbsg_dgm

what: forestsearch: Exploratory Subgroup Identification in Clinical Trials with Survival Endpoints — forestsearch-package
title: forestsearch: Exploratory Subgroup Identification in Clinical Trials with Survival Endpoints — forestsearch-package
text: Implements statistical methods exploratory subgroup identification clinical trials survival endpoints. Provides tools identifying patient subgroups differential treatment effects using machine learning approaches including Generalized Random Forests (GRF), LASSO regularization, exhaustive combinatorial search algorithms. Features bootstrap bias correction using infinitesimal jackknife methods address selection bias post-hoc analyses. Designed clinical researchers conducting exploratory subgroup analyses randomized controlled trials, particularly multi-regional clinical trials (MRCT) requiring regional consistency evaluation. Supports accelerated failure time (AFT) Cox proportional hazards models comprehensive diagnostic visualization tools. Methods described León et al. (2024) doi:10.1002/sim.10163 .

title: ForestSearch Bootstrap with doFuture Parallelization — forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture
text: Two bias correction approaches implemented: Method 1 (Simple Optimism): $$H_{adj1} = H_{obs} - (H^*_{*} - H^*_{obs})$$ \(H^*_{*}\) new subgroup HR bootstrap data \(H^*_{obs}\) new subgroup HR original data. Method 2 (Double Bootstrap): $$H_{adj2} = 2 \times H_{obs} - (H_{*} + H^*_{*} - H^*_{obs})$$ \(H_{*}\) original subgroup HR bootstrap data.

title: ForestSearch Bootstrap with doFuture Parallelization — forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture

text: data data.frame containing input dataset base simulation continuous_vars Character vector continuous variable names standardized included covariates factor_vars Character vector factor/categorical variable names converted dummy variables (largest value reference) continuous_vars_cens Character vector continuous variable names used censoring model. NULL, uses continuous_vars. Default NULL factor_vars_cens Character vector factor variable names used censoring model. NULL, uses factor_vars. Default NULL set_beta_spec List elements 'set_var' 'beta_var' manually setting specific beta coefficients. Default list(set_var = NULL, beta_var = NULL) outcome_var Character string specifying name outcome/time variable event_var Character string specifying name event/status variable (1 = event, 0 = censored) treatment_var Character string specifying name treatment variable. NULL, treatment randomly simulated 50/50 allocation subgroup_vars Character vector variable names defining subgroup. Default NULL (subgroups) subgroup_cuts Named list cutpoint specifications subgroup variables. See Details section flexible specification options draw_treatment Logical indicating whether redraw treatment assignment simulation. Default FALSE (use original assignments) model Character string: "alt" alternative model subgroup effects, "null" null model without subgroup effects. Default "alt" k_treat Numeric treatment effect modifier. Values >1 increase treatment effect, <1 decrease . Default 1 (modification) k_inter Numeric interaction effect modifier treatment-subgroup interaction. Default 1 (modification) n_super Integer specifying size super population generate. Default 5000 select_censoring Logical. TRUE (default), fits censoring distribution observed censoring times data using survreg AIC-based selection among Weibull log-normal models (without covariates). FALSE, model fitted; censoring distribution specified entirely cens_params. Default TRUE. cens_type Character string specifying censoring distribution type: "weibull" "uniform". Controls parametric family considered select_censoring = TRUE, determines required structure cens_params select_censoring = FALSE. Default "weibull". cens_params Named list censoring distribution parameters. Interpretation depends select_censoring cens_type: select_censoring = TRUE Ignored; parameters estimated data. select_censoring = FALSE, cens_type = "uniform" Must supply min max. either absent, defaults 0.5 * min(y) 1.5 * max(y) message. select_censoring = FALSE, cens_type = "weibull" Must supply mu (log-scale location) tau (scale). Optionally supply type ("weibull" "lognormal"); defaults "weibull". Censoring treated intercept-(covariate treatment dependence): lin_pred_cens_0 = lin_pred_cens_1 = mu. Default list(). seed Integer random seed reproducibility. Default 8316951 verbose Logical indicating whether print diagnostic information execution. Default TRUE standardize Logical indicating whether standardize continuous variables. Default FALSE spline_spec List specifying spline configuration treatment effect. Must include 'var' (variable name), 'knot', 'zeta', 'log_hrs' (vector length 3). Default NULL (spline)

title: Prepare Censoring Model Parameters — prepare_censoring_model
text: lin_pred_cens_0 lin_pred_cens_1 store covariate contribution — .e. \(\gamma_c' X\), intercept \(\mu_c\) excluded.  matches convention used outcome model (lin_pred_0, lin_pred_1 = \(\gamma' X\), intercept) computed calculate_linear_predictors(). simulate_from_dgm() reconstructs full log-censoring time : $$\log C = \mu_c + \delta + \tau_c \epsilon + \gamma_c' X$$ \(\mu_c\) = params$censoring$mu, \(\delta\) = cens_adjust, \(\tau_c\) = params$censoring$tau, \(\gamma_c' X\) = lin_pred_cens_{0|1}. select_censoring = TRUE, predict(survreg, type = "linear") returns full linear predictor \(\mu_c + \gamma_c' X\).  stored intercept \(\mu_c\) therefore subtracted writing lin_pred_cens_*, simulate_from_dgm() can add params$censoring$mu exactly .  Omitting subtraction causes \(\mu_c\) counted twice, producing astronomically large censoring times universal censoring. select_censoring = FALSE Weibull/lognormal cens_type, intercept-model zero covariate contribution, lin_pred_cens_0 = lin_pred_cens_1 = 0.  Storing mu instead 0 causes double-counting.
